problem:
$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)={x}^{2}(t)-6x(t)+2y(t)+9 \\ {y}^{′}(t)=4x(t)-{y}^{2}(t)+y(t)-12\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the system of ODEs above. An equilibrium point of the system is $[3,\,0]^{T}.$ Which of the following is the system obtained by shifting this equilibrium to the origin?
worked_solution:
To shift the system's equilibrium from ${x}^{∗}$ to the origin, we define the deviation vector

$$
u=x-{x}^{∗},
$$

where $x=[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}]$ and $u=[\begin{aligned}u(t) \\ v(t)\end{aligned}].$

In our case, we have

$$
u=x-[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\,⇒\,x=u+[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\,\text{and}\,{x}^{′}={u}^{′}.
$$

In coordinate form, this can be written as follows:

$$
x(t)=u(t)+3,\,y(t)=v(t),\,{x}^{′}(t)={u}^{′}(t),\,{v}^{′}(t)={y}^{′}(t).
$$

Let's now substitute these into the given system.

- Substituting into the first equation, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t) & ={x}^{2}(t)-6x(t)+2y(t)+9 \\ {u}^{′}(t) & =(u(t)+3)^{2}-6(u(t)+3)+2v(t)+9 \\  & =({u}^{2}(t)+6u(t)+9)-6u(t)-18+2v(t)+9 \\  & ={u}^{2}(t)+2v(t).\end{aligned}
$$

- Substituting into the second equation, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(t) & =4x(t)-{y}^{2}(t)+y(t)-12 \\ {v}^{′}(t) & =4(u(t)+3)-{v}^{2}(t)+v(t)-12 \\  & =4u(t)+12-{v}^{2}(t)+v(t)-12 \\  & =4u(t)-{v}^{2}(t)+v(t).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the shifted system is the following:

$$
{\begin{aligned}{u}^{′}(t)={u}^{2}(t)+2v(t) \\ {v}^{′}(t)=4u(t)-{v}^{2}(t)+v(t)\end{aligned}
$$
